{{short description|American mathematician}}
'''Michael T. Anderson''' (born November 18, 1950, in [[Boulder, Colorado]])<ref name="Who p. 105">''Who's Who in America'' 2008 Ed., Vol. 1, p. 105</ref> is an American mathematician. He is a professor of mathematics at the [[State University of New York at Stony Brook]].<ref>[http://www.math.sunysb.edu/~anderson/ Michael Anderson]</ref> His research concerns [[differential geometry]] including [[Ricci curvature]] and [[minimal surface]]s.

After doing his undergraduate studies at the [[University of California, Santa Barbara]],<ref name="Who p. 105"/>
Anderson received his Ph.D. from the [[University of California, Berkeley]] in 1981 under the supervision of [[H. Blaine Lawson]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=32072|title=Michael Anderson}}</ref>

In 2012, Anderson became a [[fellow]] of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2014-12-20.</ref>

==Major publications==
* Anderson, Michael T.; [[Richard Schoen|Schoen, Richard]]. ''Positive harmonic functions on complete manifolds of negative curvature.'' Ann. of Math. (2) 121 (1985), no. 3, 429–461. 
* Anderson, Michael T. ''Ricci curvature bounds and Einstein metrics on compact manifolds.'' J. Amer. Math. Soc. 2 (1989), no. 3, 455–490.
* Anderson, Michael T. ''Convergence and rigidity of manifolds under Ricci curvature bounds.'' Invent. Math. 102 (1990), no. 2, 429–445.
